title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding transforms a categorical variable into a set of binary variables. Each category becomes a column, and a row has a $$1$$ in the column corresponding to its category and 0s elsewhere. How does this affect the rank of the matrix?

title: Adding an Intercept Term
text: When you add a column of all ones to a matrix, it represents the intercept term in a regression model. Consider how this column interacts with the other columns in terms of linear independence.

title: Linear Independence and Rank
text: The rank of a matrix is determined by the number of linearly independent columns. Think about how the columns a, $$b$$, c, and the intercept column relate to each other. Are any of them linear combinations of the others?

hintAnswer: The columns are linearly dependent because one column can be expressed as a combination of others.
title: Evaluating Column Independence
text: Which of the following statements is true about the columns in the new design matrix?
choices: The columns are linearly dependent because one column can be expressed as a combination of others.
The columns are linearly dependent because they are all identical.
The columns are linearly independent because they all have different values.
